description: A Nintendo Entertainment System emulator: it runs a game ROM, draws the console's picture on a screen, brings its five sound channels out as separate jacks, and takes gates for the two controllers

params.text: Sets the speed the emulated processor is run at, four octaves either side of the console's own 1.789773 MHz, which raises or lowers both the pace of the game and the pitch of its sound
Scales the clock CV and can invert it, -100% to +100%, before that voltage is added to the clock speed knob
Sets the level of the first square wave voice, 0% to 200%
Sets the level of the second square wave voice, 0% to 200%
Sets the level of the triangle voice, 0% to 200%
Sets the level of the noise voice, 0% to 200%
Sets the level of the sampled-sound voice, 0% to 200%
Sets the level of the mixed output, 0% to 200%
Copies the whole state of the emulation into a single store inside the module, replacing whatever was stored before
Puts the emulation back to the stored state, and does nothing until a state has been stored
Freezes the emulation while it is held down: no processor cycles are run and every output holds the voltage it last had
Restarts the game, as the Reset button on the console does; the stored state is kept

A rising edge past 2V copies the whole state of the emulation into a single store inside the module, replacing whatever was stored before

outputs.text: A square wave with a 50% duty cycle, 10V high and 0V low, one cycle per emulated video frame of 29781 processor cycles, which is about 60Hz at the default clock speed
The first square wave voice on its own; patching a cable here takes that voice out of MIX
The second square wave voice on its own; patching a cable here takes that voice out of MIX
The triangle voice on its own; patching a cable here takes that voice out of MIX
The noise voice on its own; patching a cable here takes that voice out of MIX
The sampled-sound voice on its own; patching a cable here takes that voice out of MIX
The voices whose own jacks are empty, each at the level of its own knob, added together and scaled by the MIX knob

notes: the module does nothing until a game is loaded: right-click the panel and choose Load ROM, or drag a .nes file onto the panel. Until then the screen is black and every output stays at 0V.
there is one store for the emulator state, not a bank of them, and each save replaces the last. The store is written into the patch file, so it survives closing and reopening Rack.
Initialize on the module's right-click menu unloads the game as well as clearing the stored state, so the ROM has to be loaded again afterwards.
the emulator reads iNES format files and runs cartridges using the NROM, MMC1, UNROM and CNROM mappers; any other mapper raises an error dialog and nothing is loaded.
CV Genie (Input) goes immediately to the right of this module and writes values straight into the running game's memory.
menu: Load ROM — opens a file chooser for an iNES .nes file and starts that game running
